teaser.text: OpenText Corporation sells software that helps organizations control information, connect to business partners, and protect digital work. Its business is a flow: customers pay for software and continuing services, while OpenText spends that revenue on delivery, people, and the systems that keep the software useful.

stock.opening: OpenText's weighted forecast is 9.53 CAD in October 2027 and 25.11 CAD in October 2029, with 25% bear, 55% base and 20% bull. It hinges on free cash flow after stock pay, cloud bookings converting into cRPO and recognized revenue, customer renewals, and debt reduction.
stock.closing: The full OpenText memo also covers its business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could OpenText's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is 9.53 CAD in October 2027, a 67% loss including dividends. It rises to 16.83 CAD in October 2028, still a 41% loss. By October 2029, it reaches 25.11 CAD, an 11% loss including dividends.
The range is unusually wide. The bear case reaches zero at every date, while the bull case reaches 63.32 CAD by October 2029. The bear case receives 25%, the base case 55%, and the bull case 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for OpenText?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow after stock pay is the central operating driver. OpenText generated 726.881 million dollars on this measure in FY2026, up from 582.556 million in FY2025, but the short history is not stable. Management guides FY2027 free cash flow to 625–725 million dollars, including its investment programme. The base case uses 590 million in October 2027, then 630 million and 670 million as cloud bookings convert gradually. The bear case falls to 510 million and then 440 million because support declines, renewals weaken and investment takes longer to repay. The bull case reaches 635 million first, then 730 million and 830 million, requiring stronger bookings conversion, savings and seller productivity. Cloud revenue grew 5.5%, cRPO 10% and enterprise cloud bookings 22.5%, but constant-currency revenue excluding divestitures fell 0.5% and cloud renewal was 94%.

blocks.heading: How much cash does OpenText really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow is the cash left after customers pay and the company pays employees, suppliers and tax authorities. OpenText defines free cash flow by subtracting capital expenditure. In FY2026, US$1,006,817 thousand of operating cash flow less US$199,300 thousand of capital expenditure produced US$807,517 thousand of free cash flow.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for OpenText today?

paragraphs.text: A low forward P/E means investors pay little for forecast earnings, but forecasts can fail and accounting earnings are not the same as spendable cash. FY26 operating cash flow was US$1,006.8 million. After capital expenditure, free cash flow was US$807.5 million, against dividends of US$268.4 million. That coverage looks comfortable, but the remaining cash must also fund software investment and debt repayment.

blocks.heading: How much does OpenText pay per share over the years shown?

paragraphs.text: The dividend begins at 1.12 dollars per share because the latest quarterly rate was 0.28 dollars. The base case raises it to 1.16 dollars and then 1.20 dollars, below the recent five-year pattern of increases. The bear case holds it at 1.12 dollars before cutting to 0.84 dollars. The bull case reaches 1.20 dollars and then 1.28 dollars. The lower cash-flow outlook and high debt justify restraint, although FY2026 free cash flow covered 268.4 million dollars of dividends.

blocks.heading: How has OpenText’s revenue and profit trended over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: The last eight quarters show gradual cloud progress, not a company-wide acceleration. Support remained a drag, while licence sales made individual quarters uneven. The specialist’s question is whether cloud growth, renewals and constant-currency revenue can eventually overcome the legacy decline.
OpenText’s direct profitability improved, but reported earnings still carry the marks of an acquisition-heavy company.

blocks.heading: What should OpenText investors watch on November 5, 2026?

paragraphs.text: On November 5, 2026, OpenText reports the September quarter. The important evidence will be collections, core cloud demand and seller productivity, not just revenue against quarterly guidance. Because management plans to stop reporting enterprise cloud bookings separately, current remaining performance obligations, or cRPO, will become more important. cRPO is contracted revenue expected within roughly the next year, but it is not cash.
